questions.q: Match each situation to the storage that suits it best.
pairs: A film sold in a shop for people to take home
Optical, because the discs are cheap to produce in huge numbers
Work carried between school and home in a pocket
Solid state, because it is small, light and has no moving parts
Years of backups kept in a cupboard at low cost per gigabyte
Magnetic, because it is the cheapest way to hold a great deal
The drive a laptop boots and runs from
Solid state, because it is fast and survives being carried about
questions.feedback: Match the characteristic to what the situation actually needs. Capacity, cost, portability and durability pull in different directions.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.2 Lesson 5 — Pick the storage, station 1: How to choose

questions.q: A company needs 40 TB of storage for a server in a machine room, at the lowest possible cost. Which should it choose?
questions.feedback: Nothing is being carried anywhere, so portability and shock resistance do not matter. Cost per gigabyte is what is left, and magnetic wins it.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.2 Lesson 5 — Pick the storage, station 1: How to choose

questions.q: A school is choosing storage for the laptops pupils carry between lessons. Explain why solid state storage suits this better than magnetic.

markPoints.concept: solid state has no moving parts, so being knocked about does not damage it
accept: no moving parts|nothing moves|no head|no platter|no disc|solid state
markPoints.exemplar: Solid state storage has no moving parts, so being knocked about does not damage it.

markPoints.concept: and it is lighter, smaller and uses less power than a magnetic drive
markPoints.exemplar: It is also lighter and uses less power, which matters on a laptop.

questions.example: A laptop carried between lessons gets knocked, and a magnetic drive has a head floating over a spinning platter that a knock can wreck. Solid state storage has no moving parts at all, so it survives the handling, and it is lighter and kinder to the battery as well.
questions.paraphrase: Because nothing inside it moves, the drive is not harmed by the bumps a carried machine takes, and it also weighs less and draws less power.
questions.feedback: No moving parts, and one other advantage. Speed is a fair second mark too.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.2 Lesson 5 — Pick the storage, station 1: How to choose

questions.q: Solid state storage is always the right choice because it is the fastest.
questions.feedback: It is the most expensive per gigabyte. For 40 TB of backups in a cupboard, speed is not what matters.
